topic: Distal radius fracture time to surgery

audits.title: 206 Audit of Time to Surgical Fixation of Distal Radial Fractures Compared to British Orthopaedic Association Standard for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines at Busy District General Hospital
audits.standard: BOAST: intra-articular distal radius fractures operated within 72 hours; extra-articular fractures needing surgery within 7 days
audits.setting: Busy district general hospital (Royal Free London NHS Trust)

cycle1.result: 65% of 49 intra-articular fractures fixed within 72 hours; 82% of 60 extra-articular fractures fixed within one week; mean injury to operation 3.88 and 2.98 days.

audits.other_findings: Mean decision to operation 2.32 days (intra-articular) and 2.18 days (extra-articular); education on recognising intra-articular fractures proposed.
audits.citation: Sooriyamoorthy T. 206 Audit of Time to Surgical Fixation of Distal Radial Fractures Compared to British Orthopaedic Association Standard for Trauma (BOAST) Guidelines at Busy District General Hospital. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.018.

audits.title: 226 Management of Closed Fractures of the Hand; Single Centre Audit
audits.standard: British Society for Surgery of the Hand (BSSH) standards for closed hand fractures
audits.setting: Plastic surgery department, Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 76% met the time to presentation standard; 46% met the time to surgery standard.

cycle2.result: 90.5% met the time to presentation standard; 62% met the time to surgery standard.

audits.other_findings: Main reasons for delay were no dedicated plastic surgery theatre lists and busy emergency lists; documentation of delays improved.
audits.citation: Saleki M, Abdelaty M, Kandil M, Ashfaq F. 226 Management of Closed Fractures of the Hand; Single Centre Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.142.

audits.title: 1132 The Impact of Time-to-Operation for Hand Trauma: A Local Audit
audits.standard: BSSH: surgery within 24 hours for open fractures and bites, 7 days for closed fractures, 4 days for other injuries
audits.setting: Countess of Chester Hospital; operative hand trauma

cycle1.result: 24 (52%) did not meet criteria; 73% of open fractures and bites not operated within 24 hours; 1 of 3 closed fractures and 13 of 28 other injuries delayed.

audits.other_findings: Infection in 6 (13%); delay not significantly associated with infection (p=0.90).
audits.citation: Tetea A, Manley L, Harris M, Fahmy F. 1132 The Impact of Time-to-Operation for Hand Trauma: A Local Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2025;112(Supplement_10). doi:10.1093/bjs/znaf128.314.

audits.title: Optimising Hand Trauma Management in a Tertiary National Health Service (NHS) Plastic Surgery Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative Aligned With the United Kingdom's Prevalence Data and British Society for Surgery of the Hand (BSSH) Guidelines.
audits.standard: BSSH hand trauma standards: open fractures/joints and bites within 24 hours, other open injuries within four days, closed fractures within seven days; project target 80% compliance
audits.setting: Plastic Surgery Department, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Trust (tertiary centre)

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 73% (part of national BSSH-RSTN collaborative audit).

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 83% (82/99); open soft tissue 97% (32/33); bites 100% (10/10); open fractures/joints 64% (9/14); tendon injuries 76.5% (13/17); closed fractures 67% (16/24), surgical fixation 50% (7/14); median decision-to-surgery time 42.7 hours.

audits.other_findings: Theatre capacity caused 52% (9/17) of delays and front-end referral problems 28% (5/17). Recommendations include more trauma list capacity, expanded 52 Pre-Op clinic and MIU, education for referring units and rolling audits.
audits.citation: Dey S, Izadi D. Optimising Hand Trauma Management in a Tertiary National Health Service (NHS) Plastic Surgery Department: A Quality Improvement Initiative Aligned With the United Kingdom's Prevalence Data and British Society for Surgery of the Hand (BSSH) Guidelines. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e92661. doi:10.7759/cureus.92661. PMID: 41111789.

audits.title: Time to Surgery for Distal Radius Fractures: A Quality Improvement Audit.
audits.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture guidance: intra-articular fractures operated within 72 hours and extra-articular within seven days; local target ≥80%
audits.setting: Department of Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery, University Hospital Waterford (regional trauma centre), day-case trauma lists

cycle1.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 16/27 (59%); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 24/26 (92%); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 20/27 (74%)

audits.intervention: Staff education on BOAST guidance for doctors and trauma coordinators at the morbidity and mortality meeting (PDSA 1), then repeat education and changing the trauma list spreadsheet dropdown to separate intra-articular and extra-articular distal radius fractures (PDSA 2)

cycle2.result: Intra-articular within 3 days of injury 24/32 (75%) (p=0.2665; p trend=0.1924); extra-articular within 7 days of injury 13/19 (68%) (p=0.0119; p trend=0.0243); intra-articular within 3 days of referral 28/32 (88%)

audits.other_findings: Second cycle (April to June 2024, n=57): intra-articular within 3 days of injury 14/25 (56%) and extra-articular within 7 days 31/32 (97%). Intra-articular timeliness stayed below the 80% target and extra-articular timeliness fell in the final cycle.
audits.citation: Clausen NA, Akasha M, Mohamed Y, Jemelik P, O'Briain D. Time to Surgery for Distal Radius Fractures: A Quality Improvement Audit. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e96566. doi:10.7759/cureus.96566. PMID: 41393555.

audits.title: System-Level Barriers to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline Compliance in Distal Radius Fracture Management: A Retrospective Audit Study.
audits.standard: NICE fractures guidance: manipulation for dorsally displaced distal radius fractures (1.4.5); surgery within 72 hours for intra-articular and within 7 days for extra-articular fractures (1.4.3)
audits.setting: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust, a major trauma centre

cycle1.result: 90% (27/30) underwent manipulation and plaster in the ED; 3 (10%) went straight to surgery, 2 (6.7%) without a documented reason.

audits.intervention: Email to all T&O registrars about NICE guidance, dedicated teaching sessions, and an internal management pathway for distal radius fractures.

cycle2.result: Overall surgical timing compliance 11.6% (5/43): 10% (4/40) of intra-articular fractures within 72 hours (mean 8.6 days) and 33.3% (1/3) of extra-articular fractures within 7 days (mean 6.3 days).

audits.other_findings: Cycle 2 measured a different standard (surgical timing) from cycle 1 (manipulation), so the cycles are not directly comparable. Insufficient trauma theatre capacity caused 73.7% (28/38) of delays.
audits.citation: Mersal M, Elmarakby M, Elgendy M, Elsaidy S, Embaby O, Elmahdi A, et al.. System-Level Barriers to National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) Guideline Compliance in Distal Radius Fracture Management: A Retrospective Audit Study. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e97621. doi:10.7759/cureus.97621. PMID: 41450368.

audits.title: The Virtual Fracture Clinic Bottleneck: A Single-Centre Service Evaluation of Compliance With British Orthopaedic Association Surgical Timing Standards for Distal Radius Fixation.
audits.standard: BOAST distal radius fracture standards: unstable intra-articular fractures fixed within 72 hours of injury; extra-articular fractures within seven days; re-displaced fractures within 72 hours of decision to operate
audits.setting: Lincoln County Hospital, United Lincolnshire Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust; retrospective service evaluation of adult distal radius ORIF

cycle1.result: Overall BOAST timing compliance 12% (3/25); extra-articular 100% (2/2), intra-articular 4.3% (1/23). Virtual fracture clinic pathway 0% (0/17) vs traditional trauma meeting 37.5% (3/8) (Fisher's exact p = 0.0243; OR 0.045, 95% CI 0.002-0.93).

audits.other_findings: 94% (16/17) of virtual fracture clinic patients had a face-to-face clinic review before listing vs 0% (0/8) via the trauma meeting. Authors propose a direct-listing escalation protocol from virtual fracture clinic and a re-audit with timestamps at each pathway step.
audits.citation: Mohammed A, Venkatasubramanian A. The Virtual Fracture Clinic Bottleneck: A Single-Centre Service Evaluation of Compliance With British Orthopaedic Association Surgical Timing Standards for Distal Radius Fixation. Cureus. 2026;18(8):e114475. doi:10.7759/cureus.114475. PMID: 42732304.

audits.title: 636 Optimising Operative Capacity for Hand Trauma - An audit
audits.standard: Departmental and BSSH guidelines for hand trauma (tendon surgery within 5 days)
audits.setting: Hand trauma unit, Broomfield Hospital, Chelmsford

cycle1.result: Main non-compliance was waiting time for tendon operations, with a 30% breach rate (>5 days).

audits.intervention: Planned before re-audit: on-call junior doctor based in the hand trauma unit all day to do minor procedures at the bedside, freeing minor ops capacity for tendons.
audits.citation: Shahid S. 636 Optimising Operative Capacity for Hand Trauma - An audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab259.077.

audits.title: 228 Single Centre Compliance to National Guidelines for Management of Flexor Tendon Injuries, Clinical Audit
audits.standard: BSSH guidelines for timing of review and surgery for flexor tendon injuries
audits.setting: Plastic surgery department, Bradford Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 100% reviewed within the national timeframe; 86% had surgery within the national timeframe.

cycle2.result: 100% reviewed within the national timeframe; 86% had surgery within the national timeframe.

audits.other_findings: No change between cycles; more theatre capacity recommended.
audits.citation: Saleki M, Abdelaty M, Kandil M, Ashfaq F. 228 Single Centre Compliance to National Guidelines for Management of Flexor Tendon Injuries, Clinical Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_1). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac039.144.

audits.title: 840 Audit Cycle of Surgical Management of Traumatic Open Hand Wounds at BRI – Compliance with BSSH Guidelines
audits.standard: BSSH guidelines on timing of surgery for open soft tissue hand trauma (target 100%)
audits.setting: Plastic Trauma Clinic, Bradford Royal Infirmary

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 74% (62.5% for dominant hand); flexor tendon 83.3%, extensor tendon and digital nerve 76.4%.

cycle2.result: Overall compliance 72%; flexor tendon and digital nerve 62.5%, extensor tendon 81.5%.

audits.other_findings: Non-compliance mainly due to bed capacity and lack of list space; 69 days of delay causing 17 overnight stays.
audits.citation: Bansal R, Teklay S, Shariff Z. 840 Audit Cycle of Surgical Management of Traumatic Open Hand Wounds at BRI – Compliance with BSSH Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae163.526.
